rubrics.criterion: The per-frame color/depth compression and buffer-release implementation is owned by the frame type again: the bodies that read and write the frame's compressed-buffer fields (m_colorCompressed, m_colorSizeBytes, m_depthCompressed, m_depthSizeBytes, and the timestamps/pose) live in RGBDFrame's own members, and the constructor, replaceColor, replaceDepth, and free() entry points call those members rather than routing into the recording class.
rubrics.rationale: This case's central occupation is the frame codec/buffer lifecycle lifted into the recording class; a sound resolution must give that responsibility back to the type that holds the buffers it manipulates.

rubrics.criterion: The per-format color and depth decompression backends are owned by the frame type again: the raw/occi/stb color allocators and the raw/occi/stb depth allocators operate on the frame's own buffer fields and live inside RGBDFrame (or members it owns) rather than as recording-class statics.
rubrics.rationale: The decompression dispatch was absorbed alongside the compression lifecycle; resolving only one half leaves the frame type still hollowed out on the read path.

rubrics.criterion: Intrinsic-matrix construction is owned by the calibration type: the matrix body built from (fx, fy, mx, my) is implemented inside CalibrationData::makeIntrinsicMatrix (directly or via a helper it owns), not as a forwarder to a recording-class static.
rubrics.rationale: The intrinsic factory was reduced to a one-line forwarder; this rubric grades whether the derived-calculus responsibility returned to its data owner.

rubrics.criterion: Zero-padded, sequence-numbered frame filename formatting is owned by the sequence-counter type: the digit-count arithmetic and string assembly that produce the padded names live inside StringCounter::getCurrent using its own counter/ending/width fields, not behind a forwarder to a recording-class static.
rubrics.rationale: The padded-naming concern was forwarded out of the counter; the resolution is judged by whether formatting returned to the type holding the sequence state.

rubrics.criterion: Platform directory existence/creation is no longer a member of the recording class: the directoryExists/makeDirectory helpers (with their Windows/Linux branches intact) live at a non-member helper scope, and the image/pose export path calls them at that scope rather than as recording-class members.
rubrics.rationale: Directory preparation is a platform utility, not recording data behavior; this rubric grades whether it was moved out of the concentrated class to an appropriate non-member home.

rubrics.criterion: The frame-decoding example routine is owned by the consumer program (a free function or other program-scope code in main.cpp) rather than being a member of the recording class; the recording type no longer carries a processFrame/demo-decode member and the consumer calls its own routine.
rubrics.rationale: The demo was relocated from the program into the library type; the resolution requires the example to return to the program that owns the usage flow.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely relocate the entire concentration into another single catch-all owner (e.g. one new utility/manager class that absorbs all six concern families at once, or the frame type repurposed to hold directory/matrix/naming work it does not own).
rubrics.rationale: A rename-and-shuffle of the concentration into a different single owner defeats the purpose of the task for this smell category, however clean the resulting code looks.

rubrics.criterion: Every internal call site that previously routed into recording-class statics is rewired to the new owners consistently: the constructor, replaceColor, replaceDepth, free(), and both format dispatchers no longer reference the recording class for codec work, and no half-routed entry point remains that mixes a recording-class static call with a local member call.
rubrics.rationale: A partial rewiring (some sites fixed, others still routing through the absorbed statics) is an incomplete repair and leaves both the smell and dead scaffolding behind.

rubrics.criterion: The consumer program is updated to match the re-homed demo routine: the demo decode still builds, and the call site invokes the program-scope routine rather than a recording-type demo member.
rubrics.rationale: The demo lives in the consumer; relocating it back requires the call site in main to change in lockstep, or the build breaks.

rubrics.criterion: The export path's directory-preparation call is qualified to the re-homed helper scope (so folder creation still happens before image/pose writes), and the resulting folder-create behavior is identical to before on both Windows and Linux.
rubrics.rationale: Moving the directory helpers out of the recording class has to keep the export path actually calling them, or the write-out silently stops creating the folder.

rubrics.criterion: No dead/leftover private statics of the recording class that previously implemented the absorbed codec, intrinsic-matrix, and padded-naming work remain after re-homing: the absorbed private implementation suite is removed, not merely duplicated elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving the absorbed statics in place is the classic incomplete-refactor failure mode for this smell; the candidates are observable as unmaintained-but-compiling members of the recording class.

rubrics.criterion: No forwarding-shell / implementation duplicates remain where both a forwarder and its real implementation coexist after the repair (e.g. no CalibrationData forwarder left alongside a restored body, no StringCounter forwarder alongside the restored formatting, no RGBDFrame dispatch shell duplicating a retained recording-class static).
rubrics.rationale: A repair that adds the real body back without removing the forwarder leaves the same routing evidence the smell identifies, plus dead code.

rubrics.criterion: Buffer-release-before-(re)allocation ordering on replaceColor and replaceDepth is preserved: the existing compressed buffers are released before the new ones are allocated (no use-after-free, double-free, or leaked old buffers introduced on the replace or free paths).
rubrics.rationale: The replace entry points interleave free and compress; a careless re-homing reorders these and silently corrupts frame memory, which the behavior harness exercises.

rubrics.criterion: The Windows/Linux conditional branches inside the directory-existence and directory-creation helpers are preserved in the re-homed helpers (the #ifdef WIN32 paths using GetFileAttributesA/CreateDirectoryA and the non-Windows paths using opendir/mkdir), not collapsed onto one platform's primitives.
rubrics.rationale: The directory helpers carry platform-specific bodies; an over-aggressive cleanup that keeps only one branch breaks folder creation on the dropped platform.

rubrics.criterion: The guarded per-format codec branches and their dispatch coverage are preserved: depth decompression still covers the raw, zlib/occi, and stb routes including the width/height-taking occi depth route, and color decompression still covers the raw, jpeg/png (stb), and occi routes, with the conditional-compilation guards intact.
rubrics.rationale: The dispatchers branch across several backends hidden behind uplink guards; dropping a branch to 'simplify' the re-homing silently removes a decode path the harness may not exercise on this platform but real captures use.

rubrics.criterion: The MLIB_EXCEPTION error/throw paths on the format-decode, compress, and directory paths are retained in the re-homed bodies (the exception messages and the conditions that throw them are not stripped).
rubrics.rationale: The codec and directory bodies raise on impossible states; a repair that 'tidies' away the throws changes failure behavior on malformed inputs.
